open.description: The inset is recomputed only when InterfaceModel.subtitleSafeInset or the video size changes. It reads window.contentView.bounds and window.backingScaleFactor, which are not observable. So if the bar is revealed while a fullscreen window moves to a display with another backing scale, or the window resizes, the old point and scale values stay until the next reveal or hide. It also measures the window content view, not the video view, which is correct only while the video fills the window (fullscreen, the case it is used for).

The inset from the main window's overlays is applied to every vout of the player (vlc_player_vout_HoldAll and every VOUT_STARTED, any order). That includes secondary vouts of a multi-video-track input, which have no overlay. The impact is small because subtitles normally render on the primary vout, but restricting it to VLC_VOUT_ORDER_PRIMARY would be more exact.
A stale doc comment remains after the rescanPlugins removal: "read once at startup and again only after a plugin rescan". No rescan path exists any more; no code references remain.

The bridge only handles overlays across the bottom centre of the picture; SubtitleSafeInset.points ignores side panels and MXRAppView reports 0 unless the bar overlays the canvas. The live finding (subtitle cut under the compact library at 640 pt, '...one, first cue.') therefore depends entirely on A-window's geometry (video to the right of the library).
